title: EU Channelizer: customer-scoped routing + exception pass-through
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: Implement a request-side 'Channelizer' that enforces EU-only routing by default, applies per-customer allow/deny exceptions, and provides an auditable emergency pass-through workflow. This ticket covers the runtime decision path, authorization handoff for exceptions, telemetry and rollout plan. The design must avoid changing visible API semantics for most customers and provide explicit headers/flags for internal operator overrides.
acceptance_criteria: 1) All requests for customers scoped to EU residency must be routed to EU-backed model pools unless an exception is approved; 2) Per-customer exception status is resolvable from the policy store and honored by the Channelizer at request time; 3) Emergency pass-throughs require a recorded justification and auto-expire; 4) Fallback model variants (quantized/low-latency variants) in non-EU regions may only be used if the customer has explicit cross-border consent or an approved escape; 5) Full audit trail stored in audit-log-s3 with searchable ids; 6) Canary rollout shows no increased 95th percentile latency > 5% and no policy mismatches for selected tenants.
design_notes: High-level design: insert Channelizer as a stateless policy-evaluator between API ingress and routing layer. Evaluation order: tenant policy -> org overrides -> global compliance gates -> emergency override -> fallback policy. Policy store: extend existing tenancy-config service with 'residency_scope' and 'exception_tokens'. Decision cache: short-lived (30s) in the sidecar to avoid per-request roundtrips under normal traffic. Emergency pass-through flow: operator requests exception via Console -> creates a timeboxed 'exception_token' with justification -> token is used by request header X-RW-EU-EX to permit cross-border routing; Channelizer verifies token against KMS-signed metadata and logs for audit. Rollback behavior: exceptions expire automatically and are revoked centrally; Channelizer rejects requests referencing expired tokens.
implementation_tasks:
- API: add internal-only header X-RW-EU-EX handling (eng/runtime)
- Policy store schema migration: add "residency_scope","exceptions","last_approved_by" fields (eng/db)
- Sidecar: implement decision cache and JSONP policy matching (eng/sidecar)
- Router: plumb Channelizer decision into routing key (region, tier, variant) (eng/router)
- Telemetry: emit metric labels policy_source={tenant,org,global}, decision={allow,deny,override}, exception_id (eng/observability)
- Audit: write structured event per decision to audit-log-s3 (eng/audit)
- Console: small admin UI to request/approve exceptions (pm/design/ux)
- Tests: unit tests for policy evaluation, integration tests for token lifecycle, e2e canary harness (qa)
migration_plan: 1) Backfill existing tenants with residency_scope via nightly job; 2) Feature-flag Channelizer to 'enabled: canary' at router level; 3) Canary: enable for 1% production traffic restricted to internal staging tenants; 4) Gradually increase traffic and add 5 enterprise customers as controlled tenants for validation; 5) Flip global flag once telemetry and audits are green for two full business days; 6) Run 48-hour rollback window where exceptions can be revoked and observed.
monitoring_and_alerting: Critical metrics: policy_mismatch_rate, exception_token_failures, channelizer_latency_ms_p95, routed_non_eu_requests_for_eu_tenants. Alerts: policy_mismatch_rate > 0.1% sustained, exception_token_failures > 5/min, channelizer_latency_p95 > baseline*1.25. Dashboards: per-tenant residency compliance view, exception token audit timeline.
